key_insight: Aligning a model’s image attention with pathologists’ viewing behavior improves prostate histopathology report generation and makes the model’s highlighted regions more clinically meaningful.
clinical_relevance: This could help pathology AI produce reports and answers that better reflect the regions experts use for diagnosis, potentially improving transparency and usefulness in prostate cancer workflows.
method: Collected a multimodal dataset of 121 prostate whole-slide images with synchronized pathologist viewport trajectories, verbal descriptions, and cursor movements.
Finetuned two report-generation models using an attention-alignment loss to match model patch attention to pathologist attention.
Tested performance on prostate cancer report generation and visual question answering with models using different internal attention mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Across five clinically relevant report components, the approach improved NLP-based metrics by an average of 10.9% and accuracy by 19.3%, while producing attention maps that more closely matched pathologist attention.
watch_item: The dataset is relatively small and task-specific, so broader validation is needed before assuming the attention-alignment gains will generalize across institutions, scanners, and pathology tasks.
paper_title: Pathologist Attention-Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
